aya2: The ankle usually rolls inwards, straining or tearing the ligaments on the outer side. Most sprains heal without surgery. Early, gradual weight-bearing, exercise and balance training support recovery and also stop the same ankle from being sprained again.

aya8: The key to preventing further sprains
aya9: When the ankle turns inwards suddenly and forcefully, the ligaments in front of and below the outer ankle bone are stretched or torn. This causes pain, swelling and bruising, and it becomes hard to put weight on the foot.
aya10: If rehabilitation is left unfinished after a sprain, the ankle can become prone to spraining again, and some people develop a frequent feeling of the ankle giving way (chronic instability).

aya18: Most sprains do not involve a fracture and do not need an X-ray. The Ottawa ankle rules were developed to identify which patients need an X-ray, and in a review that combined 27 studies, they caught 97.6% of fractures.
aya19: You need an X-ray if there is pain around the ankle together with any of the following: bone tenderness along the back edge of the lower 6 cm, or at the tip, of the inner or outer ankle bone; or being unable to take 4 steps both straight after the injury and at the examination.

aya44: Returning to sport and daily life
aya45: The pain going away does not mean your ankle has fully recovered. Returning gradually prevents further sprains.
aya46: Walk on flat ground first, then move on to light jogging, and finally to changes of direction and jumping.

aya58: Should I put weight on my sprained foot?
aya59: Yes, as far as the pain allows. The American Physical Therapy Association's guideline recommends protecting a new sprain with support such as tape or a brace, and gradually putting weight on the foot. Keeping all weight off it for a long time can slow recovery.
aya60: Do I need to have an X-ray?
aya61: For most sprains, no. According to the Ottawa rules, you need an X-ray if you cannot take 4 steps both straight after the injury and at the examination, or if there is bone tenderness along the back edge of the lower 6 cm of the inner or outer ankle bone. These rules catch almost all fractures.
aya63: Used alongside an exercise programme, repeated ice applied on and off is one of the methods the guideline lists for reducing pain and swelling. Do not put ice directly on your skin; place a thin cloth in between.
aya64: Should I wear an ankle brace?
aya65: Using support after a new sprain is recommended. For people who have had a sprain, wearing a brace during sport and doing balance exercises are also recommended to prevent further sprains.
aya66: Why do I keep spraining the same ankle?
aya67: If your balance, muscle strength and sense of where your ankle is have not fully recovered after a sprain, the ankle becomes prone to spraining again. The way to break this cycle is to keep doing balance and strengthening exercises even after the pain has gone, and to return to sport gradually.
